chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from one of his companions, raising it, said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Anger is the destruction of the wise heart.' And he (peace be upon him) said: 'He who does not control his anger does not control his intellect.'
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between anger and intellect in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies anger as 'mamhaqa' (a devouring or eroding force) that corrupts the spiritual and intellectual clarity of the wise. This teaching underscores the Shia ethical principle that emotional mastery is a prerequisite for rational governance, linking the purification of the heart directly to the preservation of intellect ('aql).

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from one of his companions, raising it, said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The anger is darkness for the wise heart’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who does not control his anger, would not (be able to) control his intellect’.
en.sarwar: 13. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn ‘Abd Allah from certain individuals of his people in a marfu’ manner has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Anger darkens the heart of a wise person.’ The Imam then said, ‘One who loses control of his anger loses his power of reason.”’
